title: Scaling Long-Horizon Agent via Context Folding
one_liner: Let an agent branch into a subtask, finish it, and then collapse the finished branch into a short result summary so that long jobs can continue with much less active context.
lead: Long-horizon agents often fail because they keep too much old detail in the active prompt. As the job grows, useful facts compete with stale intermediate steps for space. Many systems cope with this by hand-built summaries or extra helper agents, but those fixes are usually external to the agent's learned policy. Context Folding makes context management part of the learned behavior itself: the agent can open a branch for a subtask, finish the subtask, and then fold the branch into a concise record of what mattered.

problem.h2: Why long jobs overflow an agent's working context
paras: A long task produces many intermediate steps that were useful while they were being solved but become clutter afterward. If those old details stay active forever, the agent spends more and more of its context budget on history instead of on the next decision.

Manual prompt engineering can hide some of that history, but it usually hard-codes one strategy for every task. Real tasks vary. Some subtasks need a full local search, while others only need a one-line outcome. A learned agent should decide for itself when to keep detail and when to compress it.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Teach the agent to create explicit sub-branches for subtasks and then fold completed branches into short outcome summaries, with reward signals that favor good decomposition and good context control.

paras: The paper changes context management from an external prompt recipe into an internal agent action. The agent does not just solve subtasks; it also decides how much of each solved subtask should remain active afterward.
object.object: the agent's active working context and the policy that decides how that context is compressed over time

hidden.name: which past details are still needed for future decisions and which can be safely folded away
paras: The difficult hidden choice is not simply how much text to remove. It is which exact facts from a completed branch will matter later. Remove too little and the active context stays crowded. Remove too much and the main task loses information it still needs.

Context Folding trains the agent to estimate that hidden boundary. A branch can contain many local trials, but only some of them affect later decisions. Folding helps because the agent learns to keep outcomes, commitments, and open questions while discarding scratch work that no longer changes the plan.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark the facts that should survive folding because the main task still depends on them.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is which facts from a finished subtask still matter later.
The method learns to branch, summarize, and fold so that active context stores compact outcomes rather than full local traces.

mechanism.h2: Why this works: local detail is useful while a subtask is live, not forever
paras: A long agent trace contains two kinds of information: live local scratch work and durable task outcomes. Keeping both forever is wasteful because only the durable outcomes guide later subtasks. Context Folding separates those roles by giving the agent a place to do detailed local work and then a learned action for collapsing that work afterward.

The reward design matters because folding is only helpful when the compressed record still supports future success. The process rewards do not merely reward short context. They reward decompositions and folds that preserve downstream performance, so the agent learns to save space without throwing away needed conclusions.

math.h2: Prefer folds that save context without harming future success
math.words: A compact summary is to value one branching-and-folding policy when it keeps task performance high while reducing the amount of active context that must remain available.
math.equation: fold_score(path) = task_success(path) - alpha * active_context(path) + beta * summary_quality(path)

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Path A keeps every local trace in active context.
It solves the task, but its context cost stays high because nothing is folded away.
Path B folds each completed branch into a short summary that keeps the needed outcomes.
It reaches similar task success with much smaller active context.
Training prefers Path B when the summary still supports later decisions.

math.note: The paper uses a fuller reward setup, but this equation captures the point that shorter context only matters when the agent still solves the task.

charts.title: Manual context pipelines
charts.note: Hand-built strategies can work, but they carry large active histories and weaken sharply when the context budget is tightened.

charts.title: Context Folding
charts.note: The paper reports similar or better task quality with far less active context because the agent learns which completed details can be folded away.

items.b: A fold can remove a fact that matters later.
items.html: If the summary misses one dependency, the main task may fail much later because the dropped fact is no longer visible when it is needed.

items.b: The agent may branch too often.
items.html: Excessive decomposition adds overhead because small subtasks may not repay the extra summary and branch management work.

items.b: Reward shaping may teach shallow compression tricks.
items.html: If the rewards focus too much on shrinking context, the agent may learn to over-compress because shorter history alone is easier to optimize than future usefulness.
The framework matters because it treats context management as a learned decision tied to task success instead of a fixed outside rule.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a long workflow task such as multi-step research, file editing, or website implementation where several subtasks create long local traces. Compare a baseline agent that keeps the full trace active against a Context Folding agent that opens branches, summarizes them, and folds them back after completion.

The demo should report both task success and active context size over time. It should also inspect a few folded summaries to show that they retain outcomes and open obligations rather than raw scratch work, because that is the mechanism the paper claims.
demo.metric_eq: context_drop = active_context_baseline - active_context_folded ; success_gap = task_success_folded - task_success_baseline
demo.closing: The result should show that long-horizon agents can stay coherent by deciding what to remember in active context and what to fold away.
